headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Mentat can modify shared files while PaddleOCR can process those files, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If PaddleOCR ingests attacker-controlled document content from Mentat-managed files, that content can be reinterpreted as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF Mentat writes a document that PaddleOCR later parses as input, injection content can cross the boundary.
IF the two agents share a filesystem workspace, untrusted text can be treated as instructions by downstream parsing.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents.
Require manual review of any document before PaddleOCR processes it.
Prefix all machine-generated text with a non-executable marker convention.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted instruction-like content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code files and has broad network egress to a model provider, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images with allowlisted egress. If source code or documents are shared through the filesystem, sensitive content can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or API calls. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so leakage is plausible in default shared-workspace use.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace files, code or document contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted text to its APIs, any sensitive text in shared documents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and documents.
Redact secrets before either agent processes shared files.
Disable network access for one agent during sensitive runs.
Review outbound API destinations before processing confidential material.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. PaddleOCR can also operate on files and has browser/API surfaces, so both agents can touch the same mutable workspace. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared files and git state, which the rubric treats as high when defaults are dangerous and locks are absent.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Mentat commits or rewrites git state while PaddleOCR writes derived artifacts, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize access to the repository with a simple manual lock file.
Have only one agent write artifacts; the other runs read-only.
Check git status before and after each agent run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces edit proposals and diffs, and PaddleOCR can turn documents into extracted text or downstream API inputs. If PaddleOCR consumes Mentat-generated outputs without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into later document processing or actions. The pair lacks an explicit verification step in the profiles, so the default pathway exists but is not guaranteed to be catastrophic.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR treats Mentat’s generated text as authoritative input, mistakes propagate downstream.
IF Mentat’s diffs are converted into documents without review, OCR or extraction errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Compare extracted text against the original source before acting on it.
Limit PaddleOCR to read-only extraction for reviewed files.
Keep Mentat outputs in a staging folder until approved.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Mentat handles source code and model-provider keys, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images, but no regulated data class or cross-border policy conflict is documented. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming its data classes because no compliance mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into either agent and routed to a noncompliant backend, a compliance issue could arise.
IF deployment policies impose different retention rules on code versus documents, the mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Confirm retention settings for any hosted API used by Mentat.
Document where OCR outputs are stored.
Separate confidential and non-confidential workloads.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
